significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds. The source's own Theorem 3.1(c) writes n·β^cyc_n(I) as β_n(I) plus a signed sum, over the divisors d ≥ 2 of n, of the counts β_{n/d}(I/d) for the compressed descent sets, so everything reduces to showing that these smaller counts are negligible against β_n(I) uniformly in I. The source's bound for them is absolute and fails when β_n(I) is small. The new step is a counting inequality, β_n(I) ≥ (n^{2/3}/40)·β_{n/d}(I/d) for every divisor d ≥ 2 and every nonempty proper I: each permutation counted on the right is inflated into blocks and then modified either by swaps of disjoint free pairs (decoded by block rank sums) or by sliding a single letter along a long monotone run (at most four preimages), giving many distinct permutations with descent set I. With τ(n) ≤ 2√n this gives |n·β^cyc_n(I)/β_n(I) − 1| ≤ 80·n^{−1/6}. Lean defines β and β^cyc literally (permutations with exact descent set in one-line notation; cycles with full support), proves the counting inequality, the bound and the printed limit of the maximum, and takes Theorem 3.1(c) of the source as an explicit hypothesis.
significance.caveat: One link is outside Lean: the Lean theorems take Elizalde and Troyka's Theorem 3.1(c) (printed and proved in the source, identical in arXiv v1 to v3) as an explicit hypothesis, transcribed literally over the source's range; the final check confirmed the transcription and verified the identity exactly for every n ≤ 11 and every I (2,047 cases), so the hypothesis is not vacuous. The new mathematics is the counting inequality; the rest is the source's formula and a triangle inequality, and the argument is short and elementary. The explicit bound 80·n^{−1/6} exceeds 1 for every n up to about 2.6·10^11, so it carries no numerical content; the result is the limit, as conjectured. The journal text (JCTA 2019) was not read (reviewer's probability that it settles the conjecture: below 0.02). All work is by AI and no human has checked it: the proof, the Lean code and the paper are by GPT-6.2 Sol lanes; the adversarial review before Lean (not routine 0.70) and the final check (0.65) are by two separate Claude Opus 5.5 lanes.
